title: The Shared Marquee
description: Eternal Rest Funeral Home and the Everlasting Vows wedding chapel share one building, one parking lot, and one plastic letter-board sign with only one set of letters. Donna does funerals, Phil does weddings, and tonight they settle whose event gets top billing this Saturday, live, while the sign keeps losing letters.

lines.speaker: ronnie
lines.text: You're on Snazzie FM. Tonight, two local businesses who share one beautiful building have agreed to settle a little signage dispute like adults, on the air. Donna, Phil, welcome.

lines.speaker: barry
lines.text: [sigh] One building. A funeral home and a wedding chapel. In the same building, Ronnie.

lines.speaker: ronnie
lines.text: Two of life's biggest days, one convenient location. That's just good business, Barry. Donna, you called first.

lines.speaker: caller-donna
lines.text: I did, Ronnie, and I'll keep it short. The marquee out front this Saturday belongs to ME. With respect to... Phil. But those are MY letters.

lines.speaker: caller-phil
lines.text: Love is love, Donna, but the letters are shared. Always been shared.

lines.speaker: caller-donna
lines.text: ...They are not shared, Phil. <p:0.3> I bought that set in nineteen ninety-one. It spells ETERNAL REST. It has always spelled ETERNAL REST.

lines.speaker: barry
lines.text: Okay, but it's one sign, right? For both businesses?

lines.speaker: caller-phil
lines.text: One sign, Barry. One pole. We split it down the middle. Top half is mine, EVERLASTING VOWS, and the bottom is Donna's little... thing.

lines.speaker: caller-donna
lines.text: My little THING. <p:0.3> Ronnie, he takes the top because the top says BEST, and you cannot spell BEST without the E S T. And there is exactly one E S T.

lines.speaker: ronnie
lines.text: Now that does sound serious. A grieving family deserves the full word.

lines.speaker: caller-phil
lines.text: Love is love, Ronnie, but a bride deserves it more. So I borrowed the E S T off her sign on Tuesday. It's currently in BEST.

lines.speaker: caller-donna
lines.text: He admits it! On the radio! <p:0.3> So now my sign, in front of the Hendersons mourning their grandmother, reads ETERNAL R. Just R, Phil. ETERNAL R.

lines.speaker: barry
lines.text: Hang on. The funeral sign just says ETERNAL R?

lines.speaker: caller-donna
lines.text: Just R, Barry. <p:0.3> And he's at it again right now, I can see him through the window. Phil, put the L back!

lines.speaker: caller-phil
lines.text: Love is love, Donna, and love needs an L more than grief does.

lines.speaker: caller-donna
lines.text: That is MY L! Now it says ETERNA, Phil! My building says ETERNA like I ran out of money halfway through caring!

lines.speaker: caller-linda
lines.text: Hi, yes, am I on? <p:0.3> I just wanted to ask which door I was supposed to use on Saturday, because I think I went in the wrong one.

lines.speaker: ronnie
lines.text: You're on, caller. Wrong door how?

lines.speaker: caller-linda
lines.text: Well the sign just said ETERNA, so I picked a door, and there was a very kind man, and I cried to him for about ninety minutes. <p:0.3> Was that not the wedding?

lines.speaker: caller-donna
lines.text: ...Ninety minutes. <p:0.3> Phil, was she in YOUR room?

lines.speaker: caller-phil
lines.text: Love is love, Donna, but I thought she was a very emotional bride. I gave her the cake samples.

lines.speaker: caller-linda
lines.text: Oh, the cake was lovely. <p:0.3> Was that not for my uncle?

lines.speaker: barry
lines.text: Wait. <p:0.3> Hold on. Linda, where is your uncle right now?

lines.speaker: caller-linda
lines.text: They took him out the back. Same time as a big white box. I figured it was all the same event.

lines.speaker: caller-donna
lines.text: Phil. <p:0.3> Phil, did the Hendersons cake and Linda's uncle BOTH go out the back on Saturday?

lines.speaker: caller-phil
lines.text: Love is love, Donna, but we use the same trolley. We have ALWAYS used the same trolley!

lines.speaker: caller-donna
lines.text: That trolley is MINE, with respect, you can't put a wedding cake on a CASKET CART, Phil!

lines.speaker: caller-phil
lines.text: It's a SHARED cart!

lines.speaker: caller-donna
lines.text: My letters!

lines.speaker: caller-phil
lines.text: My E S T!

lines.speaker: caller-linda
lines.text: I think I left my deposit in the white box.

lines.speaker: barry
lines.text: Guys. GUYS. <p:0.3> What does the sign say right now? This second?

lines.speaker: caller-phil
lines.text: ...Hang on.

lines.speaker: caller-donna
lines.text: ...He's at the board. Look at him. He's taking the last letters.

lines.speaker: caller-phil
lines.text: Donna. <p:0.4> There's only one S left on the whole pole. <p:0.3> Both signs are down to one S.

lines.speaker: ronnie
lines.text: Well there it is, folks. Two doors, one sign, one pile of letters. Donna does the front room, Phil does the back, and Linda... Linda's coming back Saturday for whichever one's cheaper.

lines.speaker: barry
lines.text: Ronnie. <p:0.3> They only have one S left.

lines.speaker: caller-donna
lines.text: That S is MINE.

lines.speaker: caller-phil
lines.text: That S is MINE.

lines.speaker: ronnie
lines.text: Donna, Phil... that's just heritage. We'll be right back, soon as somebody figures out whose uncle is in the cake box.

lines.speaker: caller-linda
lines.text: ...Was that not the recipe?
